Forecast Discussion

High pressure is over Virginia and the Carolinas through Friday. The air is very dry. Nights are cold in valleys, and afternoons warm nicely.

An upper-level disturbance along the northern Gulf Coast spreads high clouds over us this afternoon and Friday.

Saturday, that disturbance forms low pressure east of Florida as our high moves to New England. An easterly flow between the two brings more clouds and a cooler afternoon.

The low moves north Sunday but stays off the Carolina coast. Its rain remains mostly east of us. I cannot rule out light rain late Saturday night and Sunday morning near the Blue Ridge.

A front crosses from the west Monday. I cannot rule out a passing shower with it, mostly on the west side of the Appalachians. Monday is breezy.

Tuesday is dry and colder as high pressure builds to our north.

Low pressure then develops along the Southeast coast. Rain arrives late Tuesday night, and periods of rain fall Wednesday under a chilly wedge. Colder air follows Wednesday night, changing rain to snow showers in the higher elevations. Thanksgiving looks cold, and a snow shower or two is not impossible.
